design_evaluation.summary: A polished personal tech-hub site with a strong hero, clear navigation, functional theme toggle, mobile menu, and visible keyboard focus states. Main weaknesses are the floating Voice Agent widget obscuring hero content (including the '24/7' stat) on small mobile, and reduced contrast of muted/gradient text in the light theme.
strengths: Clear visual hierarchy: large two-tone headline, supporting paragraph, stat bar (7 articles / 7 RSS / 24/7), and prominent 'Live Feed' / 'AI Lab' CTAs.
Consistent card system in the tools grid with uniform icon chips, titles, descriptions, and color-coded action links (Explore, Scan, Verify, Check).
Theme toggle works end-to-end: icon switches (gear vs. moon) and dark/light palettes are applied consistently across header, hero, and cards.
Keyboard focus is clearly visible — 'Explore' nav item shows a distinct focus outline in the ui-keyboard-focus screenshot.
Mobile menu is well-structured: full-width nav items, distinct 'Break it' danger button, and an unambiguous close (X) control.
Descriptive, verb-first CTAs (Explore →, Scan →, Verify →, Check →) make each card's interaction obvious.
issues: On small mobile (ui-small-mobile-home) the floating Voice Agent widget overlaps the stats panel, partially hiding the '24/7' value; it should collapse, shrink, or become dismissible on narrow viewports.
In the light theme, the 'Break it' nav button loses contrast (red text on light pink) and muted body/stat labels sit at low contrast against the warm background.
The 'Building Trust.' gradient headline fades toward pink on the light background, reducing legibility compared with the dark theme.
In ui-home-desktop, the AI Test Result panel clips the underlying terminal text ('workers=4' is cut off at the panel edge).
The vertical 'LIVE' badge sits at the far left edge and can be cut off by the viewport edge on narrow screens.

candidate_findings.title: article-proxy-ssrf-loopback-rejected
candidate_findings.expected: Request for url=http://127.0.0.1/ must not succeed; response must be a controlled 4xx client error with a JSON error body, must not include any content fetched from loopback, and must not expose stack traces or internal details.
candidate_findings.actual: The SSRF guard behavior is functionally correct: the server refused to fetch http://127.0.0.1/, returned a controlled JSON error body ("refused fetch: private/internal IP 127.0.0.1") with null title/image, leaked no loopback content, stack traces, or internal details, and responded quickly (~397ms), indicating no real upstream fetch occurred. However, the response status was HTTP 200 instead of an expected 4xx (400/403/422), so the documented contract of a controlled 4xx client error is not satisfied — the API uses a soft-fail 200-with-error-body pattern that violates the stated status-code expectation.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.

candidate_findings.title: chat-message-wrong-type
candidate_findings.expected: JSON error body identifying invalid message field; controlled 4xx status; no sensitive details or stack trace
candidate_findings.actual: The HTTP response itself was safe and controlled: status 400, content-type application/, parseable single-key error object ("empty_message"), no stack traces, no sensitive markers, and no 500. However, the evidence does not support the specific type-confusion expectation. The request body hash (e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855) is the SHA-256 of an empty payload, and the sanitized body excerpt is empty — so no numeric `message` was actually sent. The observed 400 with `empty_message` is the same boundary already covered by the prior empty-message test; it demonstrates general controlled error handling but provides no evidence that the server type-validates `message` against a numeric value.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.
